## Add and configure the Einstein Discovery dashboard extension

To configure and use the Einstein Discovery dashboard extension in Tableau, you will need:

- Access to a Salesforce org and Tableau Desktop, Tableau Server, or Tableau Cloud.
- An Einstein Discovery prediction definition that is deployed in Salesforce.
- Source data in Tableau with fields that match the model fields required by the Einstein Discovery prediction definition.
- A worksheet in Tableau that contains the source data for the prediction.
- Additional worksheets that can be used as filters in the dashboard.
- The Einstein Discovery dashboard extension in a dashboard.

To configure and use Einstein Discovery predictions in Tableau, you and anyone who will be viewing predictions in a Tableau workbook will need certain licenses, access, and permissions in Salesforce and Tableau. For more information, see [Requirements for access](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/einstein_discovery_predictions.htm#Requirem).

### Prepare the model and the workbook

1. Build and deploy the Einstein Discovery prediction definition that you want to use. You can also use a prediction definition that someone else has built and deployed. For more information, see [Build, Deploy, and Manage Models](https://help.salesforce.com/articleView?id=sf.bi_edd_model_about.htm&type=5) in Salesforce help.
2. Create a Tableau workbook that uses a data source with fields that can be mapped to all model fields required by the Einstein Discovery prediction definition.
3. Create a worksheet that contains the source data for the dashboard extension.  
      
    This source data must include all of the fields required by the Einstein Discovery prediction definition to predict an outcome. Also, the source data must match the granularity that the Einstein Discovery prediction definition expects. For example, if the prediction definition expects sales per individual order, then your Tableau data must include fields at the level of detail of individual orders.  
      
    - **Worksheets** support predictions for multiple rows of data (bulk predictions). The worksheet can contain the necessary fields in the Rows or Columns shelves, or on Marks card properties. The worksheet will not be visible in the dashboard; a simple view will suffice. For example, you could create a text table.  
          
        ![Table showing source data for product delivery.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/EDpredictions_sourcedata_texttable.png)  
          
        Or a basic bar chart.  
          
        ![A blank chart with a horizontal axis labeled “Annual contract quantity”](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/EDpredictions_sourcedata_barchart.png)  
          
        The worksheet used as source data for the model cannot exceed 50,000 rows of data. Fields in the view can't be Measure Names or Measure Values.
    - **Parameters** support single-row predictions. To set up the worksheet, show the parameters in the view. You don't need to add fields to the view for this worksheet. For example:  
          
        ![Example showing parameters set up for source data in a worksheet.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/EDpredictions_paramters.png)
4. Create one or more worksheets with visualizations that you can set to **Use as Filter** in the dashboard.  
      
    The visualization can use a subset of the fields used by the model. Clicking marks in these views in the dashboard will refresh the predictions in the dashboard extension.
5. Create the dashboard. In the **Objects** section, click **Floating**. From the **Sheets** section, drag the source data worksheet to the canvas. Resize and hide that sheet so users won't see it in the dashboard. Also drag one or more sheets to the canvas to serve as filters in the dashboard.  
      
    ![Example of dashboard being created with multiple sheets.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/EDpredictions_dashbrd_sheets.png)  
      
    In the Sheet object menu, set at least one worksheet with a visualization to **Use as Filter**.
    
    ![A bar chart shows the on-time performance of various suppliers, with the Use as Filter option highlighted.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/EDpredictions_useasfilter.png)

### Configure the extension

1. From the **Objects** section, select **Floating**, and then drag the **Extension** object to the dashboard canvas. In the Tableau Exchange, select **Einstein Discovery**.  
      
    Sign in to your Salesforce account. After you sign in, a web page opens asking if you want to allow your Salesforce account to access Tableau. Click **Allow** to continue, and then close the resulting tab in your browser.  
      
    On Tableau Desktop, you will need to sign in to your Salesforce account every time you use the Einstein Discovery dashboard extension. If Salesforce signs you out of your session automatically, you may need to reload the dashboard extension (click the drop-down arrow on the Extension object and then select **Reload**). This time-out setting is configurable. For more information, see [Edit Session Settings in Profiles](https://help.salesforce.com/articleView?id=sf.users_profiles_session.htm&type=5) in Salesforce help.  
      
    In Tableau Cloud and Tableau Server, you should need to sign in only once if your credentials are being saved with your Tableau account settings.
2. Configure the dashboard extension.  
      
    For **Prediction Definition**, click _Search Predictions_ and then select the name of a prediction model deployed in Salesforce.  
      
    Select **Worksheet** or **Parameters** to be the source data for the predictions. Worksheet provides predictions based on a selected mark with aggregated values. Parameters supports interactive, “what if” predictive analysis on a single set of input values.  
      
    For **Worksheet**, click **Select an Option**, and then select the name of the worksheet with the source data. For **Parameters**, no other setting is needed.  
      
    ![Form for choosing prediction definitions and data sources.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/EDpredictions_settings1.png)  
      
    Click **Proceed**.
3. Map the fields from the model to the fields in the worksheet. The extension will automatically map fields based on names when possible.  
      
    To add or change mappings, click in the search box next to a prediction field and select a name from the list of available worksheet fields or parameters.  
      
    ![Add or change mappings by clicking in the search box next to a prediction field and selecting a name from the list of available worksheet fields or parameters.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/EDpredictions_dashext_settings2.gif)  
      
    You must map all of the fields to continue to the next set of configuration settings. If you don't see a matching field listed, [try these troubleshooting steps](#Troubleshooting).  
      
    Click **Next** to continue.
4. Select options for how predictions are displayed.  
      
    ![A form to configure prediction settings.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/EDpredictions_settings3.png)  
      
    **Prediction Label**: Click the field and type a label that represents the outcome that you are predicting, for example, _Likelihood of On Time Delivery_. The deployed model name is displayed by default.  
      
    **Prediction Score Unit**: Type a symbol or text that indicates the unit for the prediction score. For example, %. If the unit should be displayed before the score, select **Unit precedes score**. For example, a currency symbol (such as $) would precede a currency amount.  
      
    **Aggregation**: Specify how you want to aggregate the selected records (**Average**, **Median**, or **Sum**) in the source data worksheet. Tableau aggregates your selected data into a single set of values, which it submits to the Einstein Discovery prediction definition as input. The granularity must match the granularity expected for the model.  
      
    **Top predictors**: Specify whether to display top predictors that impact the prediction. You can also specify the number of top predictors displayed, and whether the impact values are displayed next to each predictor.  
      
    **Top improvements**: Specify whether to display information on ways to improve the probability of the predicted outcome. You can also specify the number of improvements displayed, and whether the impact values are displayed next to each improvement. For **Improvement threshold percentage**, specify a percentage number (0-99) to display improvements only if they improve the prediction by that percentage.  
      
    **Show prediction warnings**: Specify whether to show warnings about the predictive model, such as missing values in required fields or out-of-bounds values.  
      
    Consider showing everything to start with and then fine tuning what you end up sharing with your dashboard audience.
5. Click **Done**. Tableau submits the data immediately to the target Einstein Discovery prediction definition, and then displays the result.
6. In the dashboard, make sure at least one worksheet is set to **Use as Filter**. Every worksheet in the dashboard that is set to **Use as Filter** will drive the extension to update the predictions based on the current selection.

Test your dashboard by clicking and selecting different marks and areas in the dashboard (or by selecting different parameter values) to see what outcome Einstein Discovery predicts for that subset of the data.

![The Dashboard displays dynamic predictions, key drivers, and possible ways to improve predictions based on an Einstein Discovery predictive model.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/EDpredictions_dashext_intro.gif)

Save the workbook in Tableau Cloud or Tableau Server. Or, publish the dashboard from Tableau Desktop to your Tableau Cloud or Tableau Server site to share it with more people. Explorers and Viewers with access to the same Salesforce org and an Einstein Discovery in Tableau license, a Tableau CRM Plus license, or an Einstein Predictions license will be able to use the extension.

## Troubleshoot field mapping

If a field you are expecting to use is not in the list of available fields, you might need to check the data type for the field in Tableau.

Einstein Discovery and Tableau do not always recognize dimensions, measures, and data types in the same way, so you might have to change the data type and role (dimension or measure) in the Data pane of the worksheet to match how Einstein Discovery interprets the field.

1. Close the **Extension: Einstein Discovery** window.
2. Go to the source data worksheet. In the Data pane, change the data type and role of a problematic field in Tableau to match the Einstein Discovery field data type and role in the mapping settings. After you change the data type or role, you will need to replace incorrect fields in the view with the updated fields from the Data pane.
3. In the dashboard, click the drop-down menu for the extension, and then select **Configure**. Proceed to the field mapping settings and select the fields from the list.
4. If you still don't see the fields you expect in the list, go back to the source data worksheet. Remove the fields that are missing for mapping from the Marks card, or the Rows, or Columns shelves.  
      
    Next, drag the missing fields from the Data pane to Tooltip on the Marks card.
5. Repeat Step 3 to select the fields for mapping.

# Explore your Dashboards with Tableau Agent

Tableau Agent in Dashboards is an AI assistant that can help business users:

- Get a summary of what the dashboard is about
- Get insights about the vizzes in the dashboard
- Ask deep-dive questions using natural language

As a dashboard author you can turn each capability on or off at the dashboard level. You can also configure the dashboard insights to include or exclude certain worksheets, or focus on only certain types of insights.

At this time, Tableau Agent in Dashboards can't help you build a dashboard

## Getting started

Before you can start using Tableau Agent in Dashboards, there are a few things to set up.

### General requirements

- Make sure your data sources and workbooks are optimized for AI consumption. For more information see [Tableau Agent Best Practices](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/web_author_einstein_best_practice.htm).
- Turn on Tableau Agent in Dashboards for your site.
    
    - **Tableau Cloud**: Requires Tableau Cloud+, Tableau+, or a Tableau Cloud trial site. For more information, see [Turn on AI for Tableau in Your Cloud Site](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/setup_tabAI_site_setting.htm).
    - **Tableau Server** (version 2026.3 and later): Currently in Beta. Requires you to opt in and have Tableau Server+. If using a custom gateway with OAuth authentication, Tableau Agent in Dashboards is not available. For more information, see [Turn on AI in Your Tableau Server Site](https://help.tableau.com/current/server/en-us/sites_gai_server.htm).
- Grant the AI Access and Full Data Query workbook permissions for your dashboard users. For more information, see [Prerequisites](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/dashboard_narratives_overview.htm#prerequisites).

### Dashboard consumer requirements

To access Tableau Agent in Dashboards as a user consuming a dashboard, the following must be true:

- You must be on a dashboard. Tableau Agent in Dashboards capabilities aren't available on worksheets or stories.
- You must be signed into a Tableau Cloud site with Tableau Cloud+, Tableau+, a Tableau Cloud Trial site, or a Tableau Server site (version 2026.3 or later) with Tableau Server+. Tableau Agent in Dashboards must be turned on.
- You must have the AI Access and Full Data Query permissions on each workbook where you want to use Tableau Agent in Dashboards. In Tableau Cloud, starting in version 2026.3.1, if you open a dashboard and don’t have access, you can request it (if enabled by your administrator). An email will be sent directly to the workbook author to grant you access.
- The dashboard must include at least one visualization and that viz can't be empty.

**Note**: Each capability (Dashboard Overview, Dashboard Insights, and Dashboard Q&A) can be turned on or off by the dashboard author. Which capabilities are turned on determines what you have access to on your dashboard.

## Dashboard consumers

As a dashboard consumer use these capabilities to get a summary about your dashboards, get insights, and dive deeper into the data by asking your own questions.

### Dashboard Overview

The Dashboard Overview capability helps you understand what the dashboard is about. At its core, this feature answers the question "is this dashboard what I need for my analytical question?".

In general, this feature is more useful for new users to a dashboard, or those looking for a high-level summary about what it contains. The summary may change whenever the underlying data refreshes.

![A Tableau dashboard with Tableau Agent open and showing a dashboard summary](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_overview_264.1.png)

#### Get Dashboard Overview

1. In a dashboard, click the Tableau Agent ![Tableau Agent icon.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_desktop_agent_icon.png) icon to open the Tableau Agent pane, then click Got It.
2. In that Tableau Agent pane, select Get Dashboard Overview. Starting in version 2026.3.1, you can also ask for an overview by typing in the text box.
    
    ![Tableau Agent Welcome screen for dashboard consumers.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboards_consumer_welcome_screen_264.1.png)
3. To refresh your dashboard overview, in the text box, click the + button, then select Get Dashboard Overview from the Actions menu or ask for a new overview by typing in the text box.
    
    ![Tableau Agent pane showing the Actions menu.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_actions_menu_264.1.png)

### Dashboard Insights

Dashboard Insights helps you understand the analysis on a dashboard. This feature looks at the specific vizzes in the dashboard and provides natural language insights from the data, viz-by viz. Dashboard Insights is useful for those looking for a deeper understanding of the analytical story in the dashboard. Insights may change whenever the underlying data refreshes.

**Note**: Dashboard Insights only has access to the data that's used in the dashboard (what's available when you download the dashboard). Any unused fields in your data source aren't accessible by Tableau Agent and aren't included in the insights it creates

![A Dashboard With Tableau Agent open showing a list of insights.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_insights_264.1.png)

#### Get Dashboard Insights

1. If opening the Tableau Agent pane for the first time, in a dashboard, click the Tableau Agent ![Tableau Agent icon.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_desktop_agent_icon.png) icon. Then click Got It.
2. Select Get Dashboard Insights. Starting in version 2026.3.1, you can also ask for insights by typing in the text box.
    
    ![Tableau Agent Welcome screen for dashboard consumers.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboards_consumer_welcome_screen_264.1.png)
3. If you are on an existing dashboard, and already requested a Dashboard Overview, do one of the following:
    
    - Click the + button, then select Get Dashboard Insights from the Actions menu.
    - Ask for dashboard insights by typing in the text box.
        
        ![Tableau Agent pane showing the Actions menu.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_actions_menu_264.1.png)

### Dashboard Q&A

Dashboard Q&A lets you dive deeper into the data on your dashboard as well as the underlying datasource. Using the text box you can ask questions about your data using natural language.

#### Supported question types

There are several main actions available to Tableau Agent to support user requests and questions, including:

- **Slice and dice with dimensions**: "Show me the breakdown of admissions to the emergency department by speciality and triage severity."
- **Filter on dimensions or measures**: "How many of those visits were for patients under 18 who ended up admitted?"
- **Work with dates**: "What was the average wait time during the first week of June 2025?"
- **Compare multiple measures and dimensions**: "By location, how did our CSAT scores compare with our wait times for May, June, and July this year vs last year?"
- **Get data-backed hypotheses of why something happened**: "What impacted the improved CSAT scores at Meadowbrook in May?"
- **Drill down into details**: "How many of the high CSAT scores were from shifts when a therapy dog was present?"

Avoid asking about general knowledge or factors outside the dashboard. For example, Tableau Agent wouldn't be able to accurately answer "Are my profits impacted by the stock market?" unless you have stock data in your data source.

![A Tableau dashboard with tableau Agent open and showing text and table results in response to a question about the data.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_Q_A_264.1.png)

#### Data value sampling

To improve responses, Tableau Agent needs to understand not only your data set’s field names, but also the specific text values contained within those fields. Starting in version 2026.3.1, when you launch Tableau Agent, it will automatically sample your data.

**How sampling works**

1. **Automatic background scanning**: When you open Tableau Agent in a dashboard session, Tableau Agent starts sampling text fields in the background. After they are sampled, data values are cached and reused for subsequent sessions to optimize performance, automatically re-scanning after 24 hours (or when data source structure changes).
2. **Status notifications**: Tableau Agent displays an in-line indicator while scanning is actively in progress. After it’s complete, this indicator dismisses automatically.
3. **Immediate interaction**: You don’t need to wait for sampling to finish before asking a question. However, if you wait until the scanning is complete, responses may be improved.

**What data is sampled?**

- **Text dimensions**: Up to 50 categorical/text dimensions per data source.
- **Value limit**: Up to 100 distinct sample values per text field.
- **Excluded fields**: Hidden fields, ID/key columns (for example: fields ending in \_id or \_uuid), numeric measures, and dates are excluded.
- **Security & row-level security (RLS)**: Sampling runs strictly under your active user credentials, ensuring RLS is preserved. Unauthorized values are never sampled or exposed.

#### Filters

Starting in version 2026.3, Tableau Agent may suggest relevant dashboard filters, in the form of a Filter chip, as additional context when you ask a question in the text box.

**What's included in a Filter chip**:

- **Included**: Filters with a visible control on the dashboard (including parameter controls that impact or drive a viz filter) or filters shared across dashboard sheets.
- **Excluded**: Viz-local filters without a visible UI control or cross-sheet sharing. However viz-local filters are still passed in the background as context to the AI engine.

**Note**: Tableau Agent uses all filters included in the dashboard when creating dashboard overviews or insights.

![Tableau Agent pane showing the filter chip in the text box.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_qa_filter_chip.png)

- In the text box, click on the Filter chip to see the list of filters that are included.
- You can override dashboard context filters if your question is referencing a field for that specific viz.
- Filter context is captured from a snapshot of the workbook state when your question is submitted, not updated live. If you change a filter after asking a question, but before getting an answer, the answer reflects the filter state at submission time, and the chip should indicate that.
- Click the X on the Filter chip if you don’t want to include these filters as context for your request.

#### Ask questions about your data

1. If opening the Tableau Agent pane for the first time, in a dashboard, click the Tableau Agent ![Tableau Agent icon.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_desktop_agent_icon.png) icon. Then click Got It.
2. In the text box, type your question using natural language.
    
    **Note**: Dashboard Q&A requires you to have both the AI Access and Full Data Query permissions to use this capability. Starting in version 2026.3.1, if enabled by your administrator, you can request access directly in the Tableau Agent pane. An email will automatically be sent to your workbook author to grant you access. For more information, see [Permissions](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/permissions.htm#DashboardAgent).

Tableau Agent will return a response in a table format or even a viz (version 2026.3 and later) that you can hover over to view tooltips for the marks.

![Tableau Agent pane showing a visualization in the response window.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_qa_viz_response_264.1.png)

- Use the pop out ![Tableau Agent pane popout icon.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_qa_popout_icon.png) option (version 2026.3 and later) at the top of the Tableau Agent pane to pop out the pane into a floating window.
    
    ![Tableau Agent pane shown as popped out of the pane into a floating window.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_qa_popout.png)
- If the response is taking too long, you can click the Stop request option (version 2026.3 and later) in the text box and try your question again.
    
    ![Tableau Agent pane showing the Stop request option in the text box.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_qa_stop_request.png)
- If the response is incorrect and you want to troubleshoot the response, you can copy the technical details to send to your administrator. For more information, see [Troubleshoot Tableau Agent results](#Troubleshoot-results).

## Dashboard authors

**Tip**: To get the best results from Tableau Agent, make sure your data is optimized for LLM consumption. See [Improve response quality for Dashboard Q&A](#improve_response) and [Tableau Agent Best Practices](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/web_author_einstein_best_practice.htm).

As a dashboard author, Tableau Agent must be used on an existing dashboard, it can't help you build a dashboard. To access Tableau Agent in Dashboards, navigate to a dashboard tab in the authoring environment of a workbook and click the Tableau Agent ![Tableau Agent icon.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_desktop_agent_icon.png) icon in the toolbar. This opens the pane. Accept the disclaimer to continue.

With the Tableau Agent pane open on a dashboard, you have multiple options. You can:

- Click a button to see the dashboard overview or insights
- Ask for an overview or insights (version 2026.3.1 and later) or ask questions about your data using the text box
- Configure the Tableau Agent settings

### Turn on Tableau Agent in Dashboards for consumers

To allow your dashboard users to access the Dashboard Overview, Dashboard Insights, and Dashboard Q&A capabilities, you must grant them AI Access and Full Data Query permissions. By granting these permissions to your users, all capabilities are turned on by default and available on the dashboard.

In Tableau Cloud, starting in version 2026.3.1, if enabled by the administrator, users can also request access directly in the Tableau Agent pane. When they click the Request Access button, an email is automatically sent to the Dashboard Author if this option is configured for your site. For more information, see [Configure AI in Tableau](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/setup_tabAI_site_setting.htm#configure-ai-in-tableau).

You can customize Tableau Agent capabilities per dashboard, turning each on and off as needed.

1. In a dashboard, in authoring mode, click the Tableau Agent ![Tableau Agent icon.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_desktop_agent_icon.png) icon to open Tableau Agent. If this is the first time opening the pane, click Got it.
2. At the bottom of the Tableau Agent pane, click Configure Settings.
    
    ![Tableau Agent pane showing the welcome message and two buttons to Get Dashboard Overivew and Get Dashboard Insights.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_welcome_screen_auth_264.1.png)
3. For each capability, select the toggle button next to Show on this dashboard.
    
    ![Tableau Agent Configure Settings pane when opened from a dashboard.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_configure_settings_264.1.png)

### Improve response quality for Dashboard Q&A

_Supported in Tableau Cloud (Tableau Cloud+ or Tableau+) version 2026.2.6 and later_

To help Tableau Agent provide more accurate, organization-specific answers during Dashboard Q&A, you can configure business preferences to curate data source metadata available to the agent.

Business preferences allow you to provide rules, instructions, or default behaviors to help Tableau Agent answer business-specific questions about your data sources (such as "products are in stock when quantity\_on\_hand is positive" or "default year to fiscal year"). Business preferences explain how a business uses data.

Business preferences apply at the workbook level. When you upload business preferences to a workbook, Tableau Agent will refer to the business preferences document for any dashboard associated with that workbook.

**Note**: Starting in version 2026.3.1, you can upload, view errors, and edit workbook level business preferences directly in your workbook.

#### Business Preference levels

Starting in version 2026.3, Tableau Agent in Dashboards can integrate with Tableau Knowledge to ingest global business preferences. Tableau Knowledge is an enterprise knowledge management solution that helps AI agents understand your organization's data and business context by connecting Tableau Cloud content and business knowledge into live knowledge graphs. For more information see [About Tableau Knowledge](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/tableau_knowledge_about.htm).

**Note**: To enable Tableau Agent in Dashboards to ingest global business preferences defined in Tableau Knowledge, Tableau Knowledge must be turned on in the Site settings. Tableau Knowledge is available in Tableau Cloud only. For more information see [Turn on AI in Your Tableau Cloud Site](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/setup_tabAI_site_setting.htm).

Business preferences can be applied at either the Global level (via Tableau Knowledge) or the workbook level:

**Global business preferences** (Tableau Knowledge):

- Created and managed directly within Tableau Knowledge to apply across an entire knowledge graph.
- Tableau Agent uses global business preferences when processing and answering user requests if the workbook is included as a node in the knowledge graph and that graph is the default graph.
    
    Global preferences defined in Tableau Knowledge are used by Tableau Agent during query routing and execution, but they are not displayed when retrieving or viewing the list of workbook-level business preferences in Tableau.

**Workbook-level business preferences**:

- Uploaded directly to a specific workbook from Tableau Agent in the Dashboards Configuration Settings.
- Tableau Agent uses these preferences when responding to queries within that workbook's dashboards.
- Workbook business preferences are visible and accessible when requesting or managing the list of preferences in the workbook settings.
- When you upload business preferences to a workbook, Tableau Agent will refer to the business preferences document for any dashboard associated with that workbook.
- If your site uses Tableau Knowledge, Tableau Knowledge automatically ingests workbook-level business preferences when the workbook is published and includes them in the workbook node if it is included in the knowledge graph.

#### Business Preferences file requirements

**Note**: To upload a business preferences file, you must be granted AI Access permissions on the workbook and have write/edit permissions for the underlying workbook or Published Data Source (PDS).

When creating a business preferences file, make sure it meets the following requirements:

- **File formats**: Supported file types are text files (.txt) and Markdown files (.md).
    
    **Note**: Tableau Knowledge global document uploads also support .pdf, .docx, and .csv files.
- **Structure**: Start each preference item on a new line starting with #. Tableau Agent reads this line item as the header. All text following the header until the next # is treated as part of that preference and counts as one preference.
- **Item limit**: Supports up to 50 preferences (or up to 8,000 characters).
    
    **Note**: The 8,000-character limit starts from the first valid preference header and includes whitespace (front matter excluded). If a file exceeds 8,000 characters, preferences are loaded in order up to that limit. Also, total file size (including front matter) cannot exceed 500K.
- **Metadata header** (optional): You can include a YAML front-matter block between triple hyphens (---) at the top of the file to describe usage. This block is saved as part of the file, but ignored by Tableau Agent.

To help you create a Business Preferences file you can download an example file and use it like a template, replacing the suggested content with your own content.

![Markdown file example showing sample business preferences used by Tableau Agent in Dashboard Q&A.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_business_preferences_sample.png)

#### Tips for creating business preferences

Follow these guidelines when creating your business preferences document:

- **Keep it short**: Write concise, simple instructions to avoid confusing the agent.
- **Include business specific knowledge**: Define domain-specific rules, unique terminology, or custom metrics (e.g., "default year to fiscal year").
- **Be explicit and specific**: Describe unique domain logic clearly. Reference exact field names and specify how calculations apply so Tableau Agent doesn’t have to guess your schema or semantic model.
- **Avoid conflicts**: Creating workbook-level business preferences that conflict with global business preferences defined in Tableau Knowledge can be confusing to the agent.
- **Avoid ambiguity**: Eliminate duplicate or overlapping rules. Make each line item distinct so Tableau Agent can apply them consistently.
- **Break down complex instructions**: Split multi-step or intricate logic into individual, bulleted preferences to improve response accuracy

For more tips and best practices, see “Create Business Preferences” in [Tableau Agent Best Practices](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/web_author_einstein_best_practice.htm#create-business-preferences).

#### Considerations and limitations

- Publish the workbook to save the uploaded business preference document as part of your configuration settings. If the workbook node also exists in Tableau Knowledge, then the workbook-level business preferences are updated there as well. Uploaded files aren’t saved when you close a draft.
- If you publish a new update to Tableau Cloud from Tableau Desktop, the Business Preference file will be removed. Download the Business Preferences file first before publishing any updates, then upload it again.
- Undo and Redo are not currently supported. If you upload the wrong file, you can’t use Undo to revert to the previous state. You’ll need to cancel your editing session, and reopen it to upload a different file.
- Business preferences documents currently only apply to the Dashboard Q&A capability.

#### Upload or manage business preferences

1. In a dashboard, in authoring mode, click the Tableau Agent ![Tableau Agent icon.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_desktop_agent_icon.png) icon to open Tableau Agent. If this is the first time opening the pane, click Got it.
2. At the bottom of the Tableau Agent pane, click Configure Settings.
3. Under Dashboard Q&A, verify that Show on this dashboard setting is toggled on.
    
    ![Tableau Agent Configure Settings pane showing the Dasboard Q&A configuration options for Business Preferences.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_business_preferences_config_264.1.png)
4. Under Configure Business Preferences, click Edit.
5. In the Workbook Business Preferences dialog, do one of the following:
    
    - **Download an example**: Click the drop-down arrow next to Upload File, and select Download an example to get a template showing how to structure your preferences file.
    - **Upload a file**: Select Upload file, select your .txt or .md file, and click open.
    - **Download file**:Click the drop-down arrow next to Upload File, and select Download file.
    - **Replace an existing file**: Click Upload File to replace the existing file.
    - **Remove business preferences**: Click the delete icon to delete the uploaded preferences file.
        
        ![Workbook business preferences dialog showing uploaded business preferences with errors.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_business_preferences_config_errors_264.1.png)
6. Publish your dashboard to save your uploaded file to the workbook.

### Configure Insight Settings

To modify the default settings for Dashboard Insights, click Configure Settings at the bottom of the pane to open the Configure pane.

**Worksheets**

The Included Visualizations area lists all the worksheets in the dashboard. Clear the check box for any vizzes you don't want the Dashboard Insights capability to consider.

![Tableau Agent Dashboard Agent confgurations pane showing the included visulations section.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_narratives_config_included_visualizations.png)

**Insight Types**

Tableau Agent supports a number of insight types. If Tableau Pulse is enabled in the Tableau Cloud site, additional insight types will be available. Not all insight types will be evaluated for all vizzes. For example time comparisons won't be available unless there's a continuous date dimension present.

The Insight Types area lists what descriptive analysis Tableau Agent looks for in each viz. If you don't want a specific insight to be included in the output, clear the check box for that insight type. Clearing a check box prevents that insight type from being assessed for the entire dashboard. You can't configure insight types for a specific viz.

![Tableau Agent Dashboard Narratives configuration pane showing included insight types.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_narratives_config_included_insights.png)

For more details on what each insight type does, click the information icon in the UI or see "Dashboard Insights" in [Tableau Agent for Dashboards](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/dashboard_narratives_overview.htm).

### Test your output

As a dashboard author, you can use Tableau Agent in Dashboards while in the authoring environment. This can be useful to verify that a dashboard presents the analysis you expect and has a clear data story.

It's also important to test the output if you plan to turn this feature on for your consumers to ensure everything looks as it should..

## Tips for getting the best results

- Use the [Tableau Agent Best Practices](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/web_author_einstein_best_practice.htm) checklist to make sure your data source, workbooks, and dashboard are optimized for Tableau Agent.
- Upload business preferences to improve answer quality for Dashboard Q&A.
- Avoid duplicate field names. Duplicate field names or ones that are too similar can confuse Tableau Agent and it won't know which field to query. Make sure field names are unique, distinct and descriptive.
- Avoid overly complex dashboards. A simple grid design is best. For example, if there are a lot of overlapping floating objects, Tableau Agent may not be able to effectively understand your dashboard layout.
- Give all vizzes a title. Tableau Agent will do its best to interpret what it sees, but it's better to be explicit.
- Relative dates: Tableau Agent handles specific date ranges more reliably than relative date terms (like “last quarter” or “this year”). For example, when asking a question use “Show sales from April 1, 2026 to Jun 30, 2026” or “Filter to Q2 2026".
- Charts built with manipulations of the underlying data may send misleading information to the LLM. To reduce the impact on dashboard consumers, consider not including charts that are built with chart-specific modifications to the data.
    - For example, waterfall charts are constructed using a Gantt mark type with a negative measure to make the bar the correct length. The LLM receives the negative measure and will therefore misconstrue the direction of the mark.

## Be the human at the helm

As with all AI, it's important to review the results you get when using Tableau Agent. Tableau Agent does its best to understand your data, but it might not always get it right. When reviewing insights, always check the output for accuracy. Remember, you know your data best.

If Tableau Agent gets something wrong, you can try getting insights again. You can also provide feedback at any time on the results with the thumbs up or thumbs down buttons that show up with every Tableau Agent response.

![Tableau Agent showing a clickable thumbs up and a thumbs down icon to enale you to give feedback on the agent's response.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_feedback_264.1.png)

### Troubleshoot Tableau Agent results

Sometimes when Tableau Agent gets it wrong, providing feedback might not be enough. If you need help investigating what went wrong, starting in version 2026.3.1, Tableau Agent makes it easy for you to gather all of the technical details you might need to work with your administrator or Tableau Support agent to troubleshoot the issue.

1. At the bottom of the response that you want to troubleshoot, click the Copy details ![Tableau Agent in Dashboards Copy Details icon to copy the trace ID for a conversation response.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_copy_details_troubleshooting_icon.png) icon to open the Copy Details popover.
2. Click Copy Details. This copies the Trace ID for the session. The Trace ID can help Tableau troubleshoot the issue.
    
    **Note**: There is no feedback message showing that you copied the Trace ID, but it will be there when you paste it into your document.
    
    ![Tableau Agent in Dashboards Copy Details popover to let you copy the Trace ID for a conversation.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/tab_gai_dashboard_copy_details_troubleshooting_popover.png)
3. Paste the Trace ID into your document.

## Tableau Agent in Dashboards limitations

Tableau Agent in Dashboards has the following limitations:

- **Cross-Level measures**: Cannot compare measures across different levels of detail (e.g., comparing local loan amounts directly against a global average).
- **Parameter usage**: Passing parameter values into queries is not currently supported.
- **Fiscal Year formats**: Does not auto-detect fiscal dates set via standard Date Properties.
    - _Workaround_: Create a calculated field using a date offset, then hide the original field or add a detailed description (e.g."_Fiscal calendar date field for revenue recognition_").
- **Name filtering**: Specific queries like "customers with the last name of \[X\]" will fail.
    - _Workaround_: Query using "starting with..." or separate full names into distinct Customer First Name and Customer Last Name fields.
- **Virtual connections**: Currently Tableau Agent doesn’t understand field names when a data source uses a virtual connection. Instead the fieldNames is returned as a LUID resulting in Tableau Agent selecting the wrong fields.
- **User filters**: While Tableau Agent respects user filters applied at the data source, if user filters are applied at the workbook or view level, to maintain row level security and governance, Tableau Agent in Dashboards will not answer any questions.
- **Personalization ("My Data")**: Tableau Agent has no concept of current user identity. Asking "What are my sales?" fails.
    
    - _Workaround_: Explicitly state the user (e.g., "What are sales for salesperson = John Doe?").
- **Business preferences**: Business Preferences is not supported in the Configuration Settings pane in Tableau Desktop. If you publish a workbook using Desktop, and the existing published workbook on Tableau Cloud has business preferences, the newly published version from Desktop will overwrite and remove the existing business preferences.
    
    - _Workaround_: Use web editing, or before publishing to Tableau Cloud, download the business preferences and then upload them again.
- **Tableau Desktop**: Tableau Agent in Dashboards isn’t available when connected to Tableau Server. You can configure Tableau Agent in Dashboard settings when connected to a Tableau Cloud site with Tableau Cloud+, Tableau+, or a Tableau Cloud Trial site with Tableau Agent in Dashboards turned on. Tableau Agent in Dashboards capabilities for getting an overview, insights or asking questions using Dashboard Q&A is not supported.

# Export Data from Tableau Desktop

You can export the data in a Tableau data source, including all or part of the records from your original data. Alternatively, you can export only the portion of data used to generate the view.

**Note:** If you're using Tableau Cloud or Tableau Server, instead see [Download Views and Workbooks](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/export.htm) and [Link to a PNG, PDF, or CSV of a View](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/link_view.htm).

## Export data in the data source

After you join tables from one or more connections and make general customizations (for example, create a calculated field, pivot fields, create groups, apply data source or extract filters, etc.) to your Tableau data source, you might want to share or reuse the data in its new form. You can do this by using one of the methods listed below.

- [Export your data to .csv file](#data_csv)
- [Extract your data](#data_extract)
- [Export the data source](#data_datasource)

**Note:** The export may exclude some table calculations and level of detail expressions.

### Export your data to .csv file

Because the .csv format is one of the most simple structured formats for data, it's supported by a wide range of tools, databases, and programming languages. Exporting your data in the Tableau data source using this format creates an independent data set and can be a convenient and flexible way to share your data with others.

There are two primary ways you can export your data in the data source to a .csv file in Tableau: from the Data Source page and from the view.

- **From the Data Source page:** On the Data Source page, select Data > Export Data to CSV to export all the data in your data source to .csv file.
- **From the view:** On the sheet tab, drag a field to the Columns or Rows shelf, click the View Data icon in the Data pane, and click the Export All button.
    
    ![Export data function in Tableau.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/save_export_viewdata_exportall.png)

### Extract your data

Another way to export all of your data or a subset of your data in the data source is to create an extract (.hyper) file. An extract functions as an independent data set, which you can use to connect directly from Tableau. For more information, see [Extract Your Data](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/extracting_data.htm).

### Export the data source

After you connect to your data, you can export and save your data source as a Tableau data source (.tds) file. Saving the data source creates a shortcut to your remote data and allows you to avoid having to create a new connection to a specific data set each time. For more information, see [Save Data Sources](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/export_connection.htm).

## Export data used in the view

After you create a view, you can also export just the data used to generate that view.

The fields that are exported come from the fields on the shelves of the sheet. However, fields that function as external filters, in other words, the fields that appear only on the Filters shelf, are not included in the export. If you want to include other fields with the exported data without changing the baseline view, you can place those fields on the Detail shelf.

The various methods for exporting the data used to generate the view is listed below.

- [Export data in the view to Microsoft Access or .csv](#view_access_csv)
- [Export crosstab of data in the view to Excel](#view_crosstab)
- [Copy data in the view to clipboard](#view_copy_clipboard)
- [Copy crosstab of data in the view to clipboard](#view_copy_crosstab)

### Export data in the view to Microsoft Access or .csv

Export the data that is used to generate the view as an Access database (Windows only) or .csv file (Mac only).

1. In Tableau Desktop, select Worksheet \> Export > Data.
2. Select a location and type a name for your Access database or .csv file.
3. Click Save.
    
    If you're on Windows, the Export Data to Access dialog box displays to give you the option to immediately use the new Access database and continue working in Access without interrupting your work flow.
    
    ![A dialog box with fields for exporting data to Access.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/save_export7.png)

### Export crosstab of data in the view to Excel

You can export directly to Excel the data used to generate the view formatted as a crosstab. When you export your view as a crosstab, Tableau automatically opens the Excel application and pastes a crosstab version of the current view into a new Excel workbook.

Although this option provides a direct method for exporting your data to another application, performance of the export can be affected because it is simultaneously copying and formatting the data. If the view you are exporting contains a lot of data, a dialog box opens asking whether you want to export the formatting. In this case, if you choose to exclude the formatting from the export, performance of the export might improve.

- In Tableau Desktop: select Worksheet > Export > Crosstab to Excel.  
    If you're using a Mac, this option opens a dialog box where you can save the file. You must then manually open the file in Excel.
- In Tableau Server or Tableau Cloud, open a view or dashboard and select Download > Crosstab.  
    Select which sheets from the workbook to export data from.

### Copy data in the view to clipboard

Copy the data used to generate the view so that you can paste it into another application.

1. Create a view.
    
    ![A horizontal bar chart of customer names and sales volumes.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/save_export2.png)
2. Select Worksheet > Copy > Data.
3. Open another application, such as Word, and paste the data into the document.
    
    In this example, the fields placed on the Columns, Rows, and Color shelves are copied into the document. However, the Customer Segment field is not copied because it is an external filter because it appears only on the Filters shelf.
    
    ![A table that displays sales by customer name and category.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/save_export_copyclipboard.png)

### Copy crosstab of data in the view to clipboard

You can copy a crosstab version of a view so that you can paste or transfer the data into another application. The pasted data always appears as a crosstab, even if the initial view of the data in Tableau did not use a crosstab format.

Copying a crosstab is restricted by some general conditions:

- You must copy all records in the view. You cannot copy a subset of records.
- This option is valid for aggregated views only. It cannot be used on disaggregated views of data because a crosstab is by definition an aggregated view of data. This means the Aggregate Measures option on the Analysis menu must be selected in order for copying a crosstab to work properly.
- You cannot copy a crosstab if the view contains continuous dimensions such as continuous dates and times.
- Other restrictions may apply depending on the data in your view.

After the general conditions are met, copy the crosstab.

1. Create a view.
    
    ![A horizontal bar chart of customer names and sales volumes.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/save_export2.png)
2. Select Worksheet > Copy > Crosstab.
3. Open another application, such as Excel, and paste the crosstab.
    
    ![A spreadsheet that displays customer names and their purchase amounts by category.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/save_copy_cross2.png)

# Export Views from Tableau Desktop to Another Application

There are several ways to get views and workbooks out of Tableau Desktop and into a presentation, report, or web page.

**Note:** If you're using Tableau Cloud or Tableau Server, instead see [Download Views and Workbooks](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/export.htm) and [Link to a PNG, PDF, or CSV of a View](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/link_view.htm).

## Copy a view as an image

You can quickly copy an individual view as an image and paste it into another application, such as Microsoft Word or Excel. If you're using Tableau Desktop on macOS, a TIFF (Tagged Image File Format) image is copied to the clipboard. On Windows, a BMP (Bitmap) image is copied.

1. Select Worksheet > Copy > Image.
2. In the Copy Image dialog box, select the elements you want to include in the image. If the view contains a legend, under Image Options, select the legend layout.
3. Click Copy.
4. Open the target application and paste the image from the clipboard.

## Export a view as an image file

To create an image file that you can reuse, export the view rather than copy it. You can choose BMP, JPEG, PNG, or SVG image file formats on macOS or Windows. Note, however, that SVG substitutes Tableau fonts (Tableau Regular, Tableau Semibold, etc.) with a similar font.

1. Select Worksheet \> Export\> Image.
2. In the Export Image dialog box, select the elements you want to include in the image. If the view contains a legend, under Image Options, select the legend layout.
3. Click Save.
4. In the Save Image dialog box, specify a file location, name, and format. Then click Save.

## Export as a PowerPoint presentation

When you export a workbook to Microsoft PowerPoint format, selected sheets become static PNG images on separate slides. If you export a story sheet, all story points export as separate slides. Any filters currently applied in Tableau are reflected in the exported presentation.

**Tip:** To optimize a dashboard for PowerPoint, on the Dashboard tab, choose **Size** > Fixed Size > **PowerPoint (1600 x 900)**.

To export a workbook to PowerPoint:

1. Select **File** > **Export as PowerPoint**.
2. Select the sheets you want to include in the presentation. (Hidden sheets can also be included.)
    
    The exported PowerPoint file reflects the file name of your workbook, and the title slide states the workbook name and the date the file was generated.

**Tip**: Choose **File** > **Page Setup** to show or hide titles, views, legends, and captions for an individual sheet. (These options in the Show section aren't available for dashboards.)

## Export to PDF

To create a vector-based file that embeds the Tableau fonts, print to PDF. After customizing the layout of page elements using the File > Page Setup dialog, choose File > Print to PDF. For detailed instructions, see [Print Views from Tableau Desktop](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/printing.htm)

# External OAuth for Snowflake

Starting in Tableau 2024.3, you can use OAuth 2.0/OIDC to federate identity from an external identity provider to Snowflake.

Depending on the identity provider, there are different steps needed to configure the integration. This is a high-level overview intended to guide your configuration without providing the necessary details you'll find in your identity provider documentation. It is assumed you are familiar with configuring OAuth and understand the technical details required in setting up authentication with an external identity provider.

## Configure IDP on Snowflake

For information on configuring your IDP, see [External OAuth overview](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/oauth-ext-overview) in Snowflake's help system.

## Configure the IDP on Tableau

1. Create OAuth clients on the IDP for Tableau Desktop, and for Tableau Cloud or Tableau Server. The Desktop client enables [PKCE](https://auth0.com/docs/get-started/authentication-and-authorization-flow/authorization-code-flow-with-pkce) and uses `http://localhost` redirects.
2. Create the Tableau OAuth configuration file. For details on how to do this, see [OAuth Configuration and Usage](https://tableau.github.io/connector-plugin-sdk/docs/oauth) on [github](https://tableau.github.io/connector-plugin-sdk/docs/oauth), and examples [here](https://github.com/tableau/connector-plugin-sdk/tree/master/samples/components/oauth). We welcome additional examples for other IDPs.
    
    - Be sure to prefix the Tableau OAuth configuration IDs with “custom\_”.
        
        **Note:** OAuth config IDs have a maximum limit of 36 characters. IDs longer than this may not generate an error, but will not work.
    - If your IDP supports dynamic localhost port, disable `OAUTH_CAP_FIXED_PORT_IN_CALLBACK_URL`. If your IDP does not support this, make sure to add several localhost callback URLs to the allowlist in the configuration file and on the IDP.
3. Install the new Tableau OAuth configuration file in the OAuthConfigs folder associated with each application on desktop hosts (Tableau Desktop, Tableau Prep Builder, Tableau Bridge), and on each Tableau Server and Tableau Cloud site that will be using OAuth via site settings page. For more details, see [Custom OAuth Configs on Tableau Desktop](https://tableau.github.io/connector-plugin-sdk/docs/oauth#custom-oauth-configs-on-desktop) and [Site Level OAuth Clients](https://tableau.github.io/connector-plugin-sdk/docs/oauth#site-level-oauth-clients).

## Connect to Snowflake

When connecting, you must select OAuth and choose the OAuth configuration installed earlier.

![](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/snowflake_connect_oauth.png)

## Okta

If using Okta, it’s better to use a “custom authorization server” rather than the “org authorization server.” The custom authorization servers are more flexible. There’s a custom authorization server created by default, which is called “default”. The authorization URL should look like this:

`https://${yourOktaDomain}/oauth2/{authServerName}/v1/authorize`

![okta dashboard](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/athena_okta.png)

# Extract Your Data

A data extract is a subset of information that is saved separately from the original dataset. It serves two purposes: to enhance performance and to utilize Tableau features that may not be available or supported in the original data. By creating a data extract, you can effectively reduce the overall data volume by applying filters and setting other limitations.

After a data extract is created, it can be refreshed with the latest data from the original source. During the refresh process, you have the flexibility to choose between a full refresh, which replaces all existing content in the extract, or an incremental refresh, which only includes new rows since the previous refresh.

### Benefits of Extracts

- Handling large datasets: Extracts can handle massive amounts of data, even reaching billions of rows. This allows users to work with extensive datasets efficiently.
- Improved performance: Interacting with views that utilize extract data sources results in better performance compared to views connected directly to the original data. Extracts optimize query performance, resulting in faster data analysis and visualization.
- Enhanced functionality: Extracts provide access to additional Tableau functionality that may not be available or supported by the original data source, such as specific functions.
- Offline data access (Tableau Desktop): Extracts allow for offline access to data. This means that even when the original data source isn't available, users can still save, manipulate, and work with the data locally.

## Create an extract

There are multiple ways to create an extract, but the main approach is explained below.

1. After you connect to your data and set up the data source on the Data Source page, in the upper-right corner, select **Extract**, and then select the **Edit** link to open the Extract Data dialog box.

![The Extract option selected to show the Edit link](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/extract_radio_button.png)

3. Expand each section to see its options, or select Expand All. More information on each section is presented further on in this topic.

- **Data Storage**: change between **Logical Tables** or **Physical Tables**.
- **Filters**: set up filters to limit how much data gets extracted based on fields and their values.
- **Aggregation**: select **Aggregate data for visible dimensions** to aggregate the measures using their default aggregation. You can also select **Roll up dates** to a specified date level such as Year, Month, etc.
- **Number of Rows**: set the number of rows you want to extract. You can extract **All rows, Sample,** or the **Top** N rows.
- **Incremental refresh**: set up an incremental refresh based on a specific column and date range. You can also choose whether or not last rows are replaced or appended.

5. When finished, choose **Save Settings**.
6. Select the sheet tab. This initiates the creation of the extract.
7. Next, select a location to save the extract.
8. Enter an extract file name.
9. Select **Save**. If the Save dialog box doesn't display, see the [Troubleshoot extracts section](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/extracting_data.htm#troubleshoot).

## Extract settings descriptions

You can configure numerous settings when creating an extract.

### Data Storage

Under Data Storage you can select either logical or physical tables. Logical tables store data in one extract table for each logical table in the data source. On the other hand, physical tables store data in one extract table for each physical table in the data source.

Both the logical tables and physical tables options only affect how the data in your extract is stored. The options don't affect how the tables in your extract are displayed on the Data Source page.

For example, suppose your extract consists of one logical table that contains three physical tables. If you directly open the extract (.hyper) file that has been configured to use the default option, logical tables, you see one table listed on the Data Source page. However, if you open the extract using the packaged data source (.tdsx) file or the data source (.tdsx) file with its corresponding extract (.hyper) file, you see all three tables on the Data Source page.

#### Logical tables

Tableau uses logical tables as the default structure for storing extract data. Tableau generally recommends that you use the default data storage option, logical tables, when setting up and working with extracts. Many of the features you may want, like extract filters, aggregation, Top N, or pass-through functions (RAWSQL), are only available to you if you use the logical tables option. However, you can't append data to extracts that have more than one logical table.

If you choose the logical table option and your extract includes joins, the joins are applied when the extract is created.

#### Physical tables

This option performs joins at query time and can potentially improve performance and reduce the size of the extract file, if your data meets all of the following conditions:

- All joins between physical tables are equality (=) joins.
- The data types of the columns used for relationships or joins are identical.
- No pass-through functions (RAWSQL) used.
- No incremental refresh configured.
- No extract filters are configured.
- No Top N or sampling configured.
- No data needs to be appended to the extract.

#### Tips for working with physical tables

**Extracts that are larger than expected**: To determine if the extract is larger than it should be, the sum of rows in the extract using the Logical Tables option must be higher than the sum of rows of all the combined tables before the extract has been created. If you encounter this scenario, try using the physical tables option.

**Filtering options**: When using the Physical Tables option, other options to help reduce the data in your extract, like extract filters, aggregation, Top N and Sampling are disabled. If you need to reduce the data in an extract that uses the Physical Tables option, consider filtering the data before it’s brought into Tableau Desktop using one of the following suggestions:

- All joins between physical tables are equality (=) joins.
- Connect to your data and define filters using custom SQL. Instead of connecting to a database table, connect to your data using custom SQL instead. When creating your custom SQL query, make sure that it contains the appropriate level of filtering that you need to reduce the data in your extract. For more information about custom SQL in Tableau Desktop, see [Connect to a Custom SQL Query](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/customsql.htm).
- Define a view in the database. If you have write access to your database, consider defining a database view that contains just the data you need for your extract and then connect to the database view from Tableau Desktop.

**Row-level security with extracts**: If you want to secure extract data at the row level, using the Physical Tables option is the recommended way to achieve this scenario. For more information about row-level security in Tableau, see [Restrict Access at the Data Row Level](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/publish_userfilters.htm).

### Filters

Use filters to limit how much data gets extracted based on fields and their values.

**Note**: Extract filters on logical tables are pervasive (apply to the entire data source) for data sources with a single base table. For data sources with [multiple base tables using multi-fact relationships](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/datasource_mfr_multiple_base_tables.htm), extract filters are per-table and apply only to the logical table itself. For more information on pervasive and per table filters, see [Filter Data from Data Sources](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/filtering_datasource.htm).

### Aggregation

Aggregation allows you to aggregate measures. You can also select **Roll up dates** to a specified date level such as Year, Month, etc. The examples show how the data will be extracted for each aggregation option you can choose:

- **Original data:** Each record is shown as a separate row. There are seven rows in the original data.
- **Aggregate data for visible dimensions** _(no roll up)_**:** Records with the same date and letter have been aggregated into a single row. There are five rows in the extract.
- **Aggregate data for visible dimensions** _(roll up dates to Month)_**:** Dates have been rolled up to the Month level and records with the same region have been aggregated into a single row. There are three rows in the extract.

### Number of rows

You can extract all rows or the top N rows. Tableau first applies any filters and aggregation and then extracts the number of rows from the filtered and aggregated results. The number of rows options depend on the type of data source you’re extracting from. You might not see the sampling option in the Extract Data dialog box because some data sources don't support sampling.

**Note(s):**Any fields that you hide first in the Data Source page or on the sheet tab will be excluded from the extract. Click the **Hide All Unused Fields** button to remove the hidden fields from the extract.

### Incremental Refresh

Most data sources support an incremental refresh. Rather than refreshing the entire extract, you can configure a refresh to add only the rows that are new since the previous time you extracted the data.

For example, you may have a data source that is updated daily with new sales transactions. Rather than rebuild the entire extract each day, you can add the new transactions that occurred that day.

#### Incremental Refresh tips

Incremental Refresh:

- In Number of Rows, you need to select **All Rows**.
- Incremental Refresh isn't available if you enable Aggregation.

Advanced Settings:

- Advanced Settings aren't compatible with Filters.

## Extract tips

Save your workbook to preserve the connection to the extract

After you create an extract, the workbook begins to use the extract version of your data. However, the connection to the extract version of your data isn’t saved until you save the workbook. This means if you close the workbook without saving the workbook first, the workbook will connect to the original data source the next time you open it.

Toggle between sampled data and entire extract

When you're working with a large extract, it can be helpful to create a smaller sample of the data. This allows you to set up your view without having to run lengthy queries every time you add a field to your analysis. You can easily switch between using the sample data and the complete data source by selecting the appropriate option in the Data menu.

Don't connect directly to the extract

When you save extracts to your computer, you can directly connect to them using a new Tableau Desktop. However, it isn't recommended for a few of the following reasons:

- **The names of the tables may be different.** Extracts use special naming to ensure that each table has a unique name, which might be hard to understand.
- **You can’t update or refresh the extract.** When you connect directly to an extract, Tableau considers it as the original source of data, rather than a copy. This means you can’t link it back to your original data source.
- **The structure and relationships between tables will be lost.** The arrangement and connections between tables are stored in the .tds file, not in the .hyper file. Therefore, when you connect directly to the .hyper file, you lose this information. If you use logical tables storage for the extract, you won't see any references to the original physical tables.

Don't use an extract if you connect to a virtual connection with user functions in the data policy

If a virtual connection has a data policy that contains [User Functions](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/functions_functions_user.htm) (for example, `USERNAME()`) and you connect to it from a workbook or data source and create an extract there, the extract will contain only the rows that match the virtual connection data policy at the time the extract is created. To take advantage of a virtual connection with user functions in the data policy, use a live connection from the workbook or data source to the virtual connection instead of an extract.

### Remove the extract from the workbook

You can remove an extract at any time from the Data menu by selecting the extracted data source > Extract > Remove.

![](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/extract_remove_in_menu.jpg "The Data menu showing the data source name selected, the submenu for the data source with Extract selected, and the submenu with Remove selected. ")

When you remove an extract, you can choose to Remove the extract from the workbook only or Remove and delete the extract file. The latter option deletes the extract from your hard drive.

![Remove extract dialog box.](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/extract_remove.png)

### See extract history (Tableau Desktop)

You can see when the extract was last updated and other details by selecting a data source on the Data menu and then selecting Extract > History.

![](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/extract_properties.png)

If you open a workbook that is saved with an extract and Tableau can't locate the extract, select one of the following options in the Extract Not Found dialog box when prompted:

- Locate the extract: Select this option if the extract exists but not in the location where Tableau originally saved it. Click OK to open an Open File dialog box where you can specify the new location for the extract file.
- Remove the extract: Select this option if you have no further need for the extract. This is equivalent to closing the data source. All open worksheets that reference the data source are deleted.
- Deactivate the extract: Use the original data source from which the extract was created, instead of the extract.
- Regenerate the extract: Recreates the extract. All filters and other customizations you specified when you originally created the extract are automatically applied.

![](/tableau/current/en-us/pro/desktop/en-us/Img/extract_missing.png)

## Troubleshoot extracts

- **Creating an extract takes a long time:** Depending on the size of your data set, creating an extract can take a long time. However, after you’ve extracted the data and saved it to your computer, performance can improve.
- **Extract isn’t created:** If your data set contains a large number of columns (for example, in the thousands), in some cases Tableau might not be able to create the extract. If you encounter problems, consider extracting fewer columns or restructuring the underlying data.
- **Save dialog doesn’t display _or_ extract isn’t created from a .twbx:** If you follow the procedure before this to extract data from a packaged workbook, the Save dialog doesn't display. When an extract is created from a packaged workbook (.twbx), the extract file is automatically stored in the package of files associated with the packaged workbook. To access the extract file that you created from the packaged workbook, you must unpackage the workbook. For more information, see [Packaged Workbooks](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/save_savework_packagedworkbooks.htm).

## Extract feature updates

### Subrange refresh for incremental extracts

In Tableau versions 2024.2 and newer, you can specify an additional time period to re-extract previously extracted data and capture any changes that may have occurred. For more information, see [Refresh Extracts](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/extracting_refresh.htm).

### Incremental Refresh

Starting from version 2024.1, Tableau introduces a feature that enables users to perform incremental refreshes on extracts using a non-unique key column. There’s a new UI that supports these advanced settings.

This update also introduces an additional step in the extraction process. During an incremental refresh, Tableau first removes rows from the extract that match the previously recorded highest value. Subsequently, Tableau queries for all rows that have a value higher than or equal to the previous highest value. This approach ensures that any deleted rows are accounted for, along with any newly added ones.

### Extracts in the web

Beginning with version 2020.4, extracts are available in web authoring and content server. Now, you no longer have to use Tableau Desktop to extract your data sources. For more information, see [Create Extracts on the Web](https://help.tableau.com/current/server/en-us/datasource_extract.htm).

### Logical and physical table extracts

With the introduction of logical tables and physical tables in the Tableau data model in version 2020.2, extract storage options have changed from Single Table and Multiple Tables, to Logical Tables and Physical Tables. These options better describe how extracts will be stored. For more information, see [Extract Your Data](#storage).

### Deprecation of .tde format

When you create an extract it uses the .hyper format. Extracts in the .hyper format take advantage of the improved data engine, which supports faster analytical and query performance for larger data sets. Beginning in March 2023, extracts using the .tde format are deprecated in Tableau Cloud, Tableau Public, and Tableau Server (version 2023.1.0). Version 2024.2 is the last version that can open .tde format files. For more information, see [Extract Upgrade to .hyper Format](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/extracting_upgrade.htm).

### Changes to values and marks in the view

To improve extract efficiency and scalability, values in extracts can be computed differently from some data sources. Changes to how the values are computed can affect the way marks in your view are populated. In some rare cases, the changes can cause your view to change shape or become blank. These changes can also apply to multi-connection data sources, data sources that use live connections to filed-based data, data sources that connect to Google Sheets data, cloud-based data sources, extract-only data sources, and WDC data sources.

**Format of date and date time values**

Extracts are subject to consistent and strict rules around how date strings are interpreted through the DATE, DATETIME, and DATEPARSE functions. This affects how dates are parsed, or the date formats and patterns that are allowed for these functions. More specifically, the rules can be generalized as the following:

1. Dates are evaluated and then parsed by column, not by row.
2. Dates are evaluated and then parsed based on the locale of where the workbook was created, not on the locale of the computer where the workbook is opened.

These rules allow extracts to be more efficient and to produce results that are consistent with commercial databases.

**Common causes of changes to date/datetime values**

- Where the date is ambiguous and can be interpreted in several different ways, the date will be interpreted based on the format Tableau has determined for that column. For some examples, see [Scenario 1](#scenario1) below.
- When a function has to parse a YYYY-MM-DD (ISO) format. For an example, see [Scenario 2](#scenario3).
- When a function parses years, it’s interpreted as the following:
    - Year "07" is interpreted as "2007"
    - Year "17" is interpreted as "2017."
    - Year "30" is interpreted as "2030."
    - Year "69" interpreted as "2069."
    - Year "70" is interpreted as "1970."

**Common causes of null values**

- When a function has to parse multiple date formats in a single column. After Tableau determines the date format, all other dates in the column that deviate from the format become null values. For some examples, see [Scenario 1](#scenario1) below.
- When a function has to parse a YYYY-MM-DD (ISO) format. Values that exceed what is allowed for "YYYY," or "MM," or "DD" cause null values. For an example, see [Scenario 2](#scenario3).
- When a function has to parse date values that contain trailing characters. For example, time zone and daylight savings suffixes and keywords, such as "midnight" cause null values.
- When a function has to parse an invalid date or time. For example, 32/3/2024 causes a null value. In another example, 25:01:61 causes a null value.
- When a function has to parse contradicting inputs. For example, suppose the pattern is 'dd.MM (MMMM) y' and the input string is '1.09 (August) 2024', where both "9" and "August" are months. The result is a null value because the month values aren't the same.
- When a function has to parse contradicting patterns. For example, a pattern that specifies a mix of Gregorian year (y) and ISO week (ww) causes null values.

**Change to the number of rows**

In a live connection, Tableau respects and uses the source database's collation settings. In an extract, Tableau's own settings are used and these may be slightly different than the rules applied in the source database. The raw data remains the same, but the way that data is aggregated and shown in the UI may not agree.

Regardless of the connection type and collation settings, the total number of rows can be verified to be the same between a live connection and an extract by looking at View Data > Full Data analysis.

###### Scenario 1

Suppose you have a workbook created in an English locale that uses .hyper extract data source. The table after this shows a column of string data contained in the extract data source.
